chapter_theme: The one song at Thirupparaithurai (திருப்பராய்த்துறை): women who make the poet called vile and a body drowning in disease, and the plea that the Lord come to dwell in his breast; the praise centres on Murugan correcting Brahma's pride and giving the initiation of knowledge.

921.reading: The poet describes fragrant women whose small feet ring with anklets, whose breasts stand like two hills and whose eyes redden like Kama's arrows, lovers and deceivers who spin him about until he is called vile, and asks whether there will be a day when, with yoga growing and the body that whirls in the water of disease removed, Murugan sits within his breast. The praise names the vel that wore down the mountain and made Sura tremble, and the wondrous one who changed the pride of Brahma, maker of the world, and spoke the initiation of ancient knowledge, at Paraithurai.
921.nuance: நீசன் எனும்படியாக்கி: the women's harm is a loss of name as well as of self. நீ அகலம் தனில் வீற்றிருப்பது asks for the Lord enthroned in the breast. வேதன் அகந்தையை மாற்றி ... தீக்ஷை செப்பிய is the binding of Brahma and the teaching that followed, though Om is not named. The opening of the praise (தீர்க்க புத்திர முதல்வோனே, praised by the cloud-dark Vishnu, with a body of diamond) is obscure to me.
